paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.

model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the comparison of the number of floating-point operations (# FLOPs) for different fine-tuning methods using QAdapter. The categories are listed on the horizontal axis, labeled with "Full FT", "TAG Adapter", "MTL-FT", "QAdapter", and "Ours", in that order. The vertical axis is labeled "# FLOPs", with a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^18 to 10^20, with tick labels at 10^18, 10^19, and 10^20. The bars are colored orange, except for the last category, "Ours", which is green. The bar heights vary, with "Full FT" being the tallest at approximately 8 x 10^19, and "Ours" being the shortest at around 1.8 x 10^18. The other bars have values in between, with "TAG Adapter" at about 2 x 10^19, "MTL-FT" at roughly 1.2 x 10^19, and "QAdapter" at approximately 4 x 10^18. The bars are not sorted in any particular order other than the categorical order on the x-axis, and the green bar for "Ours" is visually distinct from the other orange bars.
model_annotations.German: This bar chart compares the number of floating-point operations (# FLOPs) for different fine-tuning methods for language models using QAdapter. The categories are listed on the horizontal axis, labeled with "Full FT", "TAG Adapter", "MTL-FT", "QAdapter", and "Ours", in that order. The vertical axis represents # FLOPs, with a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^18 to 10^20, with tick labels at each order of magnitude. The bars are colored orange, except for the last category, "Ours", which is green. The bar heights vary, with "Full FT" having the tallest bar at approximately 5 x 10^19 # FLOPs, and "Ours" having the shortest bar at around 1.5 x 10^18 # FLOPs; the other bars have values of approximately 2 x 10^19 for "TAG Adapter", 1.2 x 10^19 for "MTL-FT", and 4 x 10^18 for "QAdapter". The bars are not sorted by height, but rather follow the order of the categories on the horizontal axis, with no bars visually emphasized or annotated.
